territorial_scope.description: Applies to automated and teleoperated commercial vehicles operated in Alabama; Section 6(e) subjects a remote driver to specified Alabama provisions regardless of the jurisdiction where the remote driver is physically present.

evidence.quote: regardless of the jurisdiction in which the remote driver is physically present

summary.short: Alabama 2019 act allowing automated commercial motor vehicles to operate in the state without a conventional driver when listed criteria are met, and allowing commercial vehicles with teleoperation systems to run with a remote driver. Effective on passage and Governor approval.
summary.long: SB 47 (2019) defines automated driving and teleoperation terms and authorizes automated commercial motor vehicles to operate in Alabama without a conventional driver physically present, provided the vehicle can comply with federal and state traffic laws, is registered and titled in Alabama, is certified under 49 C.F.R. Part 567, can reach a minimal risk condition, and carries at least $2,000,000 motor vehicle liability coverage. The owner or lessee is treated as the operator for traffic-law compliance, and the automated driving system is considered licensed to operate the vehicle. Section 6 permits commercial vehicles with teleoperation systems to run without a conventional driver when a remote driver operates them. The remote driver is treated as the operator for traffic and criminal-charge purposes, must hold the required license class, is subject to alcohol and drug testing provisions regardless of location, and the vehicle must meet the Section 7 requirements, including achieving a reasonably safe state if teleoperation fails. The Department of Transportation is the sole state agency with jurisdiction over these vehicles, and political subdivisions may not impose additional requirements specific to them. Accident-reporting duties are deemed satisfied if specified steps are taken, and existing liability under common or statutory law is preserved. The Act takes effect immediately following passage and Governor approval, or on becoming law.

notes: Only one public body is named. Owner, lessee, operator, remote driver and law enforcement are functional roles, not named entities. Text as written contains errors in Section 6(e) ('remote drive', 'have give consent'), quoted unchanged. Section 2(a) says the act governs exclusively, while Section 8 preserves liability under existing law. Section 7(2) repeats the 49 C.F.R. Part 567 reference from Section 3(3). Section 9 makes the act effective on passage and approval by the Governor or on becoming law; no calendar date is stated.

evidence.quote: The motor vehicle shall be covered by motor vehicle liability coverage in an amount of not less than two million dollars ($2,000,000).
AUTOMATED COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE. A commercial motor vehicle equipped with an automated driving system.

The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific operational design domain.
A commercial motor vehicle as defined in subdivision (2) of Section 32-9A-1, Code of Alabama 1975.
A driver who manually exercises in-vehicle braking, accelerating, steering, and transmission gear selection input devices in order to operate a vehicle.

All of the real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate a vehicle in on-road traffic excluding strategic functions such as trip scheduling and selection of destinations and waypoints.
A condition to which a user or an automated driving system may bring a vehicle in order to reduce the risk of a crash

A description of the specific operating domain in which an automated commercial motor vehicle is designed to properly operate, including, but not limited to, roadway types, speed, environmental conditions, and other domain constraints.
A natural person who is not seated in a commercial motor vehicle, but is able to perform the entire dynamic driving task.
Hardware and software installed on a commercial motor vehicle that allow a remote driver to operate the motor vehicle.

obligations.summary: An automated commercial motor vehicle may operate without a conventional driver present only if it meets six criteria: federal law and state traffic-law compliance, state registration and titling, FMVSS certification under 49 C.F.R. Part 567, ability to reach a minimal risk condition, at least $2,000,000 liability coverage, and that registration does not alter liability law (criterion 6).

enforcement.note: No penalty, fine, licence sanction or other sanction regime is stated in this text. Section 6(e) makes a remote driver subject to Section 32-6-49.13, Code of Alabama 1975, and Section 6(b) refers to charges under the Alabama Criminal Code, Title 13A, and Title 32. These are cross-references without a stated penalty, so no entry is coded.
